subject: Proforma invoice held — unexpected usage spike and metering clarification
messages:
From: Jared Lu <jared.lu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Question on held proforma + spike in token usage (May)

Hi Marissa —

We received a notice that our May proforma invoice is being held for review. Our billing team flagged a ~4.7x jump in billed tokens compared to our April baseline (same production traffic, no rollout). We run a steady streaming summarization job and a nightly indexing pipeline; nothing that should cause a jump like this.

Can you help surface the raw usage export for the window 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-08 and advise if you see any duplication or session-count anomalies? Attached is a small sample from our side showing request IDs and timestamps.

We also need to know whether a provisional credit is possible while you investigate — this hit will push the invoice over our spend threshold and delay payment.

Thanks,
Jared
Billing Manager, Acme Analytics
attachments: usage_sample_202605.csv (CSV)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Lu <jared.lu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on held proforma + spike in token usage (May)

Hi Jared —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the sample. I’ve looped in Sean from Billing Ops and Monica from Customer Success to triage. High level plan:

- Sean: run a backfill on the first-week aggregation window and compare per-request tokenization/streaming counts to the raw request logs.
- Monica: coordinate temporary invoice hold/provisional credit request with finance and procurement.
- I’ll share any immediate flags we find.

We appreciate the patience — we’ll aim to provide an initial read within 48 hours.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jared Lu <jared.lu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on held proforma + spike in token usage (May)

Hi all —

I dug into the ingestion logs and reconciliation pipeline for the 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-08 window. Findings so far:

1) There was a short-lived duplication condition for streaming completions on 2026-05-02 02:13-02:22 UTC caused by an autoscaler restart on a dedicated pool. Two in-flight streams were re-acknowledged and recorded twice by the aggregation job. Estimated duplicate tokens: ~6.2M (about 18% of the observed spike).

2) Separate from the duplication, we saw a change in your client-side streaming pattern on 2026-05-03 where the SDK retried partial-chunk frames during transient network flaps — those retries were counted as new token emissions by our current metering heuristic. We have a mitigation queued to de-dupe identical stream-chunk signatures in the exporter. Estimated additional tokens from retries: ~8.5M.

3) Remaining delta (~55% of spike) appears to be legitimate: a short config rollout on your side expanded the summary length (you increased max_tokens in one service). We can correlate the request IDs you provided to verify.

Proposed remediation:
- We will mark the duplicate ingestion events and issue a provisional credit of $8,200 while we complete a full audit. The credit will appear as a memo on the May proforma; net payable will reflect the adjustment.
- We will publish a corrected per-request usage export (CSV) within 72 hours and share the reconciliation steps.

Next steps for Jared: please confirm whether you pushed a config change around 2026-05-03 and share any rollout IDs.

Attachments: invoice_202605_proforma.pdf (proforma we’re holding)

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Lu <jared.lu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Billing <billing@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on held proforma + spike in token usage (May)

Thanks Sean — that level of detail is super helpful.

We confirmed an internal rollout: a surge in max_tokens was part of a canary on 2026-05-03 (internal rollout id: CAN-314). That accounts for the legitimate portion you flagged. We also saw the SDK retry logs for 05-03 and can share a fuller request-id list if that helps with matching.

We accept the provisional credit of $8,200 while you finalize the audit. Please send the corrected per-request usage CSV and the provisional_credit_memo_0526.pdf so our accounting team can process the adjusted payment. Also confirm the timeline for a final reconciled invoice and whether the credit will be reflected in the Stripe/ACH remittance file so we can align our payment run.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Jared
Jared Lu
Billing Manager, Acme Analytics
attachments: provisional_credit_memo_0526.pdf (PDF)
